site.title: LIMS/ELN Program Specification
site.description: Explore a synthetic laboratory workflow through shared contracts, implementation examples, comparison evidence and accountable review.

release.label: 0.3.1 candidate
release.summary: The signed spec-v0.3.1 tag exists, and accepted Governance 2.1.0, Implementation 0.3.2, Simulation, and Comparison release subjects are bound with their selected-future semantics. The living Program carriers remain candidate_pending_promotion until the hosted sibling proof and post-tag release observation settle.
release.evidenceBoundary: The pages describe the living source state at the Git commit recorded in the projection manifest. A signed tag and a completed post-tag release observation are distinct facts. Hosted proof, configured environments, publication approval, and accountable acceptance retain their own evidence and decision paths.

contracts.name: Repository role and release status
contracts.summary: The release-role record states what this repository owns, the living candidate status, its contract links, the standing branch controls, and the release-specific review route. Its pending Program coordinate represents the open post-tag observation.

contracts.name: Constellation map
contracts.summary: The constellation record names all five repositories and the behavior each one owns.

contracts.name: Constellation lock
contracts.summary: The lock records each accepted sibling release subject and its decision-changing semantic bindings. The Program placeholder remains until the post-tag observation records the permanent commit and tree in the living carriers.

contracts.name: Program release observation
contracts.summary: The version-specific record starts with planned post-tag evidence fields and later carries the signed Program subject, hosted proof, merge admission, independent review, and GitHub review record from a separate observation commit.

contracts.name: Bounded operation catalog
contracts.summary: The packaged catalog gives implementation, simulation, and comparison work one versioned operation vocabulary.

contracts.name: Golden Specimen scenario
contracts.summary: The synthetic journey gives producers one executable scenario with a stable identity and one content digest used by every consumer.

contracts.name: Golden Specimen result schema
contracts.summary: The closed schema defines the decision-relevant result shape that both producers can project while retaining their own evidence detail.

Browser rendering, hosted responses, domain configuration, and publication approval remain with their fitting later observations.
